findings.description: XXE vulnerability in drawing file parser - unsafeXML parsing without XXE protection when optional dependencies are unavailable
findings.reasoning: The fromstring() function is called on untrusted XML content read directly from a ZIP archive without guaranteed XXE protection. While the code has conditional XXE protections (when LXML >= 3.3.1 or defusedxml is available), if neither optional dependency is present or if they are disabled via environment variables (OPENPYXL_LXML=False or OPENPYXL_DEFUSEDXML=False), the code falls back to standard xml.etree.ElementTree which does not disable external entity resolution by default. This allows XXE attacks when parsing malicious Excel files.

evidence.code_context: find_images() function reads drawing XML from ZIP archive and parses it with fromstring()
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Untrusted archive data flows directly to fromstring() without explicit XXE prevention in all code paths
evidence.notes: XXE protection is optional (LXML or defusedxml), not mandatory. Standard ElementTree is vulnerable by default.

findings.description: XXE vulnerability in manifest reader - unsafe XML parsing of content types without guaranteed XXE protection
findings.code_snippet:
def read_manifest(self):
        src = self.archive.read(ARC_CONTENT_TYPES)
        root = fromstring(src)
        self.package = Manifest.from_tree(root)
findings.reasoning: The read_manifest() method parses the [Content_Types].xml file from the XLSX archive using fromstring() without guaranteed XXE protection. This file is read early in the Excel parsing process and is a critical entry point. If XXE protections (LXML or defusedxml) are not available or disabled, the standard ElementTree parser will resolve external entities, allowing XXE attacks.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: Archive data (ARC_CONTENT_TYPES) flows to fromstring() which may lack XXE protection

findings.description: XXE vulnerability in Excel drawing file parser - untrusted XML from ZIP archive parsed without XXE protection when lxml/defusedxml unavailable
findings.reasoning: The code calls fromstring() on untrusted XML data read from an Excel file's drawing archive. While the codebase has conditional XXE protections (LXML with resolve_entities=False or defusedxml), when neither is available or disabled, it falls back to standard ElementTree which is vulnerable to XXE attacks. An attacker can craft a malicious .xlsx file with XXE payloads in the drawing XML to achieve information disclosure or denial of service.

findings.description: XXE vulnerability in workbook.py parser - unsafe XML parsing without XXE protections when defusedxml and safe lxml are unavailable
findings.reasoning: The fromstring() function parses untrusted XML content from a ZIP archive without explicit XXE protections.
